title: Education Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2025
short_title: Education Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would strengthen regulation of international education, change oversight of offshore higher education and introduce separate measures affecting First Nations medical students and childcare administration.
Education regulators would gain controls over providers and courses, while offshore course delivery would require authorisation and eligible First Nations medical places would be uncapped.

Separate childcare measures would expand financial information collection and data sharing, and retrospectively validate certain subsidy reconciliation decisions while waiving debts arising from timing discrepancies.
changes: Education providers would have to report commissions paid to education agents.
The internal review period for overseas education regulatory decisions would increase from 90 days to 120 days.
Demand-driven Commonwealth supported medical places for eligible First Nations students would begin from 2026.
The education department secretary could compel childcare providers that are constitutional corporations to supply financial, cost and pricing information for a delivery prices project.
summary.affected: International students, education providers and agents, eligible First Nations medical students, childcare providers and families receiving subsidies are affected.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Presented the Education Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2025 and its explanatory memorandum; the bill was read a first time.

speeches.speaker: Julian Leeser
speeches.brief: Argued that the Education Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Other Measures) Bill 2025 would address international education, Indigenous medical places, offshore higher-education regulation and childcare information powers, while seeking a Senate inquiry into the childcare provisions.

speeches.speaker: Karen Grogan
speeches.brief: Presented the seventh report of the Selection of Bills Committee and moved its adoption; amendments proposed referrals of specified bills, including environment, payday superannuation, terrorism, Defence and Fair Work legislation, to Senate committees for inquiry and report by dates ranging from 19 November 2025 to 24 March 2026.
